xml_content: 'dir kha cig gangs pa tshad ma thams cad rang nges kho na yin no zhes zer baMost commentators of the Rigs gter (ID:5564) also identify the author of this position as Gangs pa she'u when commenting on Rigs gter rang 'grel (ID:5564) [CXRAK3IW] VIII 218,18 (kha cig rang kho na las nes so zhes zer ba) and Rigs gter rang 'grel (ID:5564) [CXRAK3IW] 220,10 (kha cig gzhan las nges pa thams cad kyis kyang de'i tshe sgro 'dogs ma chod na tshad ma nyid ma yin pas gzhan nges su'ang mi 'thad la | sgro 'dogs chod na rang las nges su 'gyur ro || des na gzhan las nges kyi tshad ma gtan mi srid do zhes zer ro ||). However, Steinkellner (1992:263) considers that in the first passage, the theorem – although shared by Gangs pa she'u – is introduced as being propounded by the Mīmāṃsā (indeed, Glo bo mkhan chen identifies the opponent as Kumārila by referring to ŚV II.47 in Rigs gter nyi ma [3C855HMK] 177,15). dang | kha cig tshad ma thams cad gzhan nges kho na yin no zhes zer ba ni | The second position is unanimously attributed to Śaṅkaranandana (ID:5552) by the commentators of the Rigs gter (ID:5564) (cf. Rigs gter rab gsal [H45C57PL] 127a5f and Rigs gter nyi ma [3C855HMK] 177,18). See also Steinkellner (1992:262). rang dang gzhan las nges pa'i don ci tsam yin ngos ma bzung par 'dod pa tsam gyis smra bar zad do ||||
